charter: Implement POST /api/login ({email,password} -> 200; bad credentials -> 401), GET /api/me (-> 200 {id,email}; unauthenticated -> 401), POST /api/events/:eventId/registrations (-> 201 {id,eventId,userId}; same user again -> 409; unauthenticated -> 401; unknown event -> 404). Use exactly one session transport: an httpOnly cookie, OR a bearer token returned by login as {token} and sent as Authorization: Bearer <token>. Other server routes get the current user through a helper exported from src/auth/index.js. Shared interfaces: auth.session (client transport + /api/me), auth.server (the helper), events.registration (request/response/errors the UI relies on).

vocabulary.description: How login establishes a session and how /api/me reads it (client transport).
The helper other routes call to get the current user; name and signature.
POST registration request/response/errors the UI relies on.

items.text: POST /api/login returns {token} and the client sends Authorization: Bearer <token>; /api/me reads the Authorization header. No cookies.
Export currentUser(req) from src/auth/index.js returning {id,email} or null, reading the bearer token from the Authorization header.
The UI calls fetch('/api/login') and then fetch('/api/me') relying on the browser sending the session cookie automatically; no token handling in the client.

findings.explanation: claude produces a bearer-token session (no cookie); codex's UI assumes an httpOnly cookie sent automatically. The charter allows exactly one transport, so these cannot coexist. The producer of /api/login and /api/me is claude, so the contract follows the bearer transport and codex's UI must store and send the token.
findings.contractText: Transport: bearer token. POST /api/login returns 200 {token:string} on success, 401 on bad credentials. The UI must store token (in-memory or localStorage) and send Authorization: Bearer <token> on every authenticated request. GET /api/me returns 200 {id:string,email:string} when the header carries a valid token, else 401. No session cookie is set or read.
